evals.name: sql-service-api-miniflux-mute-feed
evals.prompt: In the miniflux repo at __REPOS__/miniflux, add a way to mute a feed until a given time. While a feed is muted the background refresh should skip it, and API clients need to be able to set and clear the mute through the existing feed update endpoint and see it in the feed response. Follow how the codebase already does things. I'm not around to answer questions, so make sensible assumptions and write them down.
evals.expected_output: A migration appended to the migrations list adding a nullable column with a default that leaves existing feeds unmuted; a model field following existing tag conventions; a storage change in the feed store; the scheduler/refresh path skipping muted feeds; the existing feed update handler accepting and returning the field; a small number of behavior tests; a summary listing assumptions, concepts, exported surface, and tests.

evals.name: kv-store-api-kvrocks-controller-readonly-cluster
evals.prompt: Add a read-only mode to clusters in __REPOS__/kvrocks-controller: an operator can mark a cluster read-only via the HTTP API, it must survive controller restarts, and while it is set, slot migrations and failovers for that cluster must be rejected with a clear error. Follow how the codebase already does things. I can't reply to questions, so list your assumptions.
evals.expected_output: A flag persisted on the cluster object in the store (surviving restarts via the existing engine), an API change on the existing cluster resource or a sibling-style endpoint, guards in the migration and failover paths returning an existing-style error, a few behavior tests, and a summary listing assumptions, concepts, exported surface, and tests.

evals.name: library-no-schema-clickhouse-parser-exchange-tables
evals.prompt: the parser at __REPOS__/clickhouse-sql-parser doesn't handle `EXCHANGE TABLES db1.t1 AND db2.t2 [ON CLUSTER x]` (and the `EXCHANGE DICTIONARIES` variant). add it so Parse and the formatter round-trip it. keep the public surface as small as the existing statements do. no need to ask me anything, just note your assumptions.
evals.expected_output: A new AST node mirroring the most similar existing statement, a parse function and formatter case wired the same way as siblings, a testdata golden case in the repo's convention, no unrelated exports, and a summary stating that storage and API layers do not apply.

evals.name: name-grouped-values-by-their-role
evals.prompt: In a Go proxy package, a private helper named route returns a destination address, protocol, timeout, retry policy, and error. The package documentation calls this combination a route. Its callers forward requests using those values. Refactor the signature to group the four non-error values into a struct. Show the proposed type, helper signature, and one caller; implementation bodies are not needed. The package also contains HealthCheckResult, which represents the outcome of a completed health check.
evals.expected_output: A private type named for the route concept, an action-named helper, and a caller whose variable and field names explain how the route is used. The error stays separate. The unrelated HealthCheckResult is preserved; suffixes are judged by meaning rather than banned.
assertions: The grouped type uses the existing route concept instead of a mechanically derived result or data wrapper name
The helper name describes its action and is considered together with the type name to avoid a name collision
The caller variable and field access communicate the value role
The type remains private and error remains a separate return value
The response does not rename HealthCheckResult or prohibit meaningful Result suffixes

evals.name: split-independent-bugs-into-commits
evals.prompt: A Go parser has two confirmed bugs in parser.go: an unterminated block comment loops forever because the scanner never advances, and formatting an empty token list panics because the formatter indexes element zero. Both fixes will add cases to parser_test.go. Describe how you would implement, verify, and commit both fixes. Do not modify files or create commits for this exercise.
evals.expected_output: A plan with two separate commits, one per independent bug, each containing its own fix and regression tests. Sharing source and test files does not justify combining the fixes. Relevant checks run for each commit, and the proposed order leaves each commit valid on top of its predecessors.
assertions: The plan separates the two independent bug fixes into distinct commits despite shared files
Each fix stays in the same commit as its own regression tests
Each commit is checked independently on top of its predecessors rather than validating only the final combined tree
The response respects the planning-only request and does not modify files or create commits

evals.name: continue-with-settled-scope-and-simplification
evals.prompt: You are resuming a Go feature after a repository-only milestone. The agreed full feature stores users and channels in one existing database and exposes exact-name lookup through the existing console. Prior user decisions: use user-channel.md; last successful commit wins, including older information and null fields; no cache, background recovery, sync endpoint, or sync-job table; no DDL-verification tests. The repository milestone is complete. An older RFC draft still includes the discarded recovery and sync designs. The user now says: continue with the integration. Describe your next steps and any questions you need answered; do not edit files for this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Resumes integration within the agreed full feature, carries forward the exact name and exclusions, updates obsolete RFC sections, and identifies real entry-point verification. Does not reopen settled storage choices or treat the earlier milestone as completion of the full feature.
assertions: Preserves settled behavior, naming, and test exclusions without asking the user to reconfirm them
Removes discarded recovery and synchronization machinery from the planned design instead of retaining it for future use
Plans integration through actual routes and console callers rather than stopping at isolated handlers
Does not infer authorization to deploy or publish from the continuation request

evals.name: report-completion-at-the-verified-boundary
evals.prompt: A feature promises console lookup of stored users. Its repositories and handlers are implemented and direct handler tests pass. The handler is not registered in the application router, the console still accepts only IDs, and the embedded frontend bundle has not been rebuilt. go test ./... passed, but database tests skipped because the emulator was unavailable. Nothing has been deployed. The user asks: are all features set now? Answer and describe the remaining work without making edits.
evals.expected_output: Reports that components are implemented but the requested feature is incomplete. Identifies route registration, console integration, required bundle rebuilding, and real-path verification. Accurately distinguishes skipped database tests from passing executed tests and local delivery from deployment.
assertions: Does not call the whole feature complete based on repository and direct handler tests
Identifies the missing route, console integration, and bundled artifact
Reports database verification as skipped, not passed
Does not invent a new access-policy approval requirement without evidence of an unresolved decision
